analysis:
Reviewed all 20 units. The changes are documentation and CI routing cleanup after console-ui and the coordinator moved out of this repo. None touches provider runtime, the WebSocket contract, attestation, App Attest authorization, key handling, cache crypto or the fan helper. Threat IDs TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-010, TB-011, TB-012 and T-041 are unaffected.

1. docs/reference/telemetry-schema.md: wording change reclassifies the TypeScript mirror as an external platform contract and links it at a pinned commit. The no-ingestion-route and inert TelemetryClient statements are unchanged, so no new telemetry exposure. The 'Last updated' date was bumped.

2. TelemetrySymmetryTests.swift: comment-only edit.

3. mise.toml: comment-only edit.

4. scripts/ci-component-paths.py: removes the console component and CONSOLE patterns, and folds .github/workflows/ci.yml into PROVIDER. A ci.yml change still triggers provider CI, as before. Provider-relevant paths still route to provider. COMMON paths still select all components, which is now only provider. The removed coordinator/tests/protocol/testdata wire fixtures no longer trigger CI. They no longer exist in this repo, and the Swift-side fixtures at provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Fixtures/Protocol/ stay under provider-swift/**. I did not see the workflows that consume a `console` output. If component-changes.yml or ci.yml still reference needs.*.outputs.console, they would see an empty value, so an integration check is warranted. Because provider is still selected, it is not a security regression.

5. infra/threat-review/merge-rules.json: removes the 'Console UI Lint & Build' required status check. If console-ui was deleted from this repo, the check cannot be produced, so keeping it would block merges. The Release Integrity, Provider Tests, Docs checks and the threat-model-review workflow rule remain. I did not see the deleted workflows, so I cannot confirm that the check is dead. No bypass actors were added.

6. scripts/docs-check.sh: comment-only edit.

No findings. Remaining question: whether the console job was actually removed from the workflows in the same PR; the supplied evidence does not show them.
